resources.string: The selected command receives the original text on stdin. Check stdout before replacing the selection.
Register a command in Commands → Snippets and enable “Offer for selected text”.
Text must be valid text without NUL, up to 64 KiB.

Choose a tab to place next to this one. It joins this tab\'s group, up to the group\'s limit. Tap a pane to focus it; drag a divider to resize. Long-press a pane title and drag it to move that tab. The button at the right end of a title (or a double-tap on the title) shows only that tab; press it again to return to the group.
Open another terminal or GUI tab first.
Show the current tab on an external display. The phone can control it or show a different tab.
Shown on the external display. The keyboard controls that session.
External display: use this area as a touchpad and the keyboard below for input.
Cannot use this display. The session is still running.

Reads the local framebuffer directly. Uses Xvfb for display and x11vnc only for input; packages are downloaded on first use. Applies to newly opened GUI tabs. Fixed starting resolution; no GPU acceleration.
Long-press GUI to split GUI and terminal

Long-press the GUI (🖥) button beside + to open session layout. Choose top/bottom or left/right and another tab to use GUI and terminal (CUI) together. The same menu restores one pane or selects an external display. A short tap opens GUI as before.
A group holds up to %1$d tabs.
Tap a tab on the right to put it in the group framed in green. Tap a tab in a group to send it back. Long-press a tab and drag to reorder it, or let go without moving to rename it.
Tap a tab on the right to add it.
Every tab is in a group.
How many tabs one group can hold. This screen allows up to %1$d (each pane keeps at least 4 rows with the keyboard open).
Long-press a tab and let go for its menu
Rename the tab, put it in a group or take it out. A group shows its tabs one above the other; tap a pane to type there. Edit groups… lays out every group and tab on one screen.
Arrange the groups, then press Start with this. Every terminal tab in every group is ticked, and input goes to all ticked tabs, whichever group they are in.
When off (the default), broadcast starts OFF so you can check the highlighted panes before sending.
Slide + / 🖥 to the left to broadcast

A 📡 button slides out. Arrange the groups and press Start with this: what you type in a ticked tab then goes to every ticked tab, in every group. The 📡 switch stays in the tab bar while broadcasting; tap it for ON / OFF, long-press it to rearrange the groups. Panes that receive input are framed in the warning colour (the theme\'s yellow). Slide again to stop.
Pinch the tab bar to widen or narrow every tab
Spread two fingers on the tab bar to show longer tab and group names, pinch them together to fit more tabs. All tabs change together, and the width is kept for next time.
Record a log of this tab
No file yet: it is created when something is first written.
